title: 07 Sasame: Japanese-minimal tea house footer
strengths: Almost nothing on the page and all of it placed: name, one sentence, three notes with kanji labels (訪 VISIT, 時 HOURS, 秋 OCTOBER NOTE), a brush enso, one vertical phrase, one seal
One typeface (Shippori Mincho) for Latin and Japanese; pale celadon paper with a faint fibre, sumi ink, matcha for the kanji labels, one vermilion
The October note ('The first hojicha of the year is roasting in the back room. Ask for a cup with roasted chestnut.') is the kind of line a real eight-seat tea house would write
slop_signals: The brush enso is the stock mark of 'Japanese minimal'; drawn with real texture, but expected
The enso floats in the centre with no relation to the columns on the left or the vertical type on the right
The middle third of the footer is empty in a way that reads as unresolved rather than as deliberate space
fixes: Anchor the enso: align its centre to the vertical phrase's column or to the top of the three notes, or shrink it and set it beside the seal
Consider a drawn object from the house instead of the enso: the kettle, a chawan, a sprig of the first hojicha
Pull the vertical phrase in one column so the right edge is not a lone strip

references.what: A Japanese brand footer that is almost empty: tracked small capitals, a JA / EN switch, no boxes; our language row follows this
One calligraphic line carries the whole footer and everything else steps back; the same single-gesture idea
One large mark with a tiny address below; a lesson in anchoring one object to the type
A compact footer with the email top-left, link columns and a language picker; the plain version of the same job

round4.pairwise: lost to VanMoof by 2 (not blind); the earlier blind test lost to Legora by 4
changed: The tea-year Gantt, seal, today line and every chart label removed
The one signature element is a seasonal sentence in Shippori Mincho beside the name, at 49 px so it reads at gallery size
Visit, Hours, Seats and More as four quiet columns; headings muted, links no longer underlined, the address reduced to 'Higashiyama 2-chome' so it cannot match a real house
Last row of the section above: 'Ask for a seat'
